B
Which property most directly distinguishes a nascent ribosome-bound chain from a completed released chain?
Its carboxyl end remains attached to tRNA|Its amino terminus is attached to the mRNA|It contains only hydrophobic residues|It has no peptide bonds
A

During elongation the growing chain is ester-linked to tRNA via its carboxyl end. mRNA provides a template, not a covalent anchor; the chain already has peptide bonds and may contain diverse residues.
B
Anfinsen's ribonuclease experiment most directly supports which conclusion?

Every protein folds without assistance in vivo|Under suitable conditions a sequence can direct recovery of its functional conformation|Disulfides specify the genetic code|ATP hydrolysis is essential for all folding
B

The recovered activity after reversible denaturation supports sequence-dependent structure for this protein. It does not establish universal spontaneous folding, a role for disulfides in decoding, or universal ATP consumption.
B
Which region of a ribosome-bound polypeptide normally emerges first?
Carboxyl terminus|Central domain only|Amino terminus|Both termini simultaneously
C
Translation extends the carboxyl end, so the amino end is made earlier and can emerge first. The C terminus stays near the peptidyl-transferase center while attached to tRNA.
B
A chaperone commonly recognizes which feature of an incompletely folded soluble protein?
A particular mRNA stop codon|A universal phosphorylated serine|A permanently buried catalytic site|An accessible aggregation-prone hydrophobic segment
D

Exposed peptide segments can serve as substrate-binding sites for Hsp70. Stop codons and phosphorylation are not universal recognition signals for this mechanism, and buried sites are not directly accessible.
B
In the conventional Hsp70 cycle, which state has slower substrate dissociation?
ADP-bound|ATP-bound|Nucleotide-free in all conditions|GTP-bound
A
ATP hydrolysis favors the more stable substrate-retaining ADP state. ATP binding promotes rapid exchange; GTP is not the standard nucleotide of this cycle.
B
What is the primary role of bacterial DnaJ in the DnaK cycle?
Directly synthesize ATP|Stimulate DnaK ATP hydrolysis and assist substrate recruitment|Cap a GroEL ring|Reduce all client disulfides
B
DnaJ is a J-domain cochaperone. GroES caps GroEL, and PDI-like oxidoreductases handle disulfide exchange; ATP synthesis is not the J-protein role.
B
GrpE participates in the bacterial Hsp70 system by doing what?
Hydrolyzing substrate peptide bonds|Recognizing stop codons|Promoting nucleotide exchange|Forming the GroEL chamber
C
GrpE promotes ADP release, allowing ATP rebinding and restoration of rapid substrate exchange. It neither cleaves the client nor participates in translation termination or chamber formation.
B
Which arrangement describes bacterial GroEL?
One ring of eight distinct subunits|A monomeric peptide-binding protein|A ribosomal 30S subunit|Two rings of seven subunits each
D
GroEL forms a tetradecamer of two heptameric rings. CCT has eight distinct subunits per ring; Hsp70 exemplifies a peptide-binding monomeric cycle rather than GroEL architecture.
B
What does GroES provide in the standard group I chaperonin cycle?
A removable lid over a GroEL chamber|The client's primary sequence|An aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase|A permanent subunit of the mature client
A
GroES caps a GroEL ring to create an enclosed folding space. It does not encode the client sequence, charge tRNA, or normally remain in the mature client.
B
Which is a characteristic of cytosolic CCT/TRiC?
Requires a separate bacterial GroES lid|Group II chaperonin with an intrinsic lid mechanism|Is identical to mitochondrial Hsp70|Always has seven identical subunits per ring
B
CCT has eight related distinct subunits per ring and an built-in closure mechanism. It is not Hsp70 and does not use the canonical bacterial GroES lid.
B
Which compartment normally favors oxidative folding of many secretory proteins?
Eukaryotic cytosol|Nucleoplasm exclusively|ER lumen|Ribosomal decoding center
C
The ER lumen contains oxidative folding machinery. Cytosol is generally reducing; a decoding center is not the compartment that establishes most secretory protein disulfides.
B
Which enzyme accelerates rearrangement of incorrectly paired cysteines in ER clients?
DNA ligase|RNA polymerase II|Peptidyl transferase|Protein disulfide isomerase
D
PDI catalyzes thiol-disulfide exchange. The other enzymes act in DNA replication/repair, transcription and translation respectively.
B
Which chemical event is catalyzed by a peptidyl-prolyl isomerase?
Cis–trans interconversion about an X–Pro peptide bond|Hydrolysis of the entire backbone|Oxidation of all cysteines|Addition of an amino acid to tRNA
A
An isomerase accelerates conformational interconversion without cutting the bond or changing sequence. Proteases, oxidoreductases and synthetases perform the other reactions.
B
Calnexin and calreticulin typically recognize what during ER glycoprotein folding?
A stop codon|A monoglucosylated N-linked glycan|A mitochondrial presequence in the cytosol|A polyadenylated RNA tail
B
These lectin chaperones recognize a glucose-containing glycan intermediate, unlike the peptide-binding BiP system. RNA and mitochondrial targeting signals are unrelated substrates.
B
Which feature distinguishes calnexin from calreticulin in their usual ER localization?
Calnexin is cytosolic only|Calreticulin is a ribosomal protein|Calnexin is membrane-associated; calreticulin is luminal and soluble|Both are secreted digestive proteases
C
Both assist ER glycoprotein maturation but differ in membrane association. Neither is a ribosomal or digestive enzyme.
B
Which statement about mature human insulin is correct?
It is a single 51-residue backbone|It has no intrachain disulfide|It is produced by translation of separate A and B mRNAs|It contains A and B chains joined by two interchain disulfides
D
The A chain has 21 residues, B has 30; two disulfides connect chains and one lies within A. Both originate from one precursor.
B
A zymogen is best defined as what?
An enzyme precursor activated by processing, commonly limited proteolysis|A protein permanently destroyed by proteolysis|A ribosome with no tRNA|A nucleotide exchange factor
A
Zymogen processing generates a functional enzyme rather than simply destroying it; the other terms describe unrelated mechanisms.
B
Which enzyme initiates physiological trypsinogen activation in the intestinal lumen?
DNA polymerase|Enteropeptidase|Hsp70|Calreticulin
B
Enteropeptidase cleaves the activation peptide. Trypsin subsequently activates more trypsinogen and other precursors; the remaining options are unrelated to digestive activation.
B
Which statement correctly describes a protein complex?
Every subunit must be identical|Every oligomer is an aggregate|Functional quaternary structure can depend on correct interfaces between separate chains|Subunits must always form disulfides
C
Specific interactions generate biological oligomers; heterooligomers exist, noncovalent association is common, and aggregation is not synonymous with assembly.
B
Which is not a necessary property of every mature protein?
Compatibility with its biological role|An appropriate chemical environment|An appropriate conformational ensemble|A single rigid globular conformation
D
Intrinsically disordered regions and dynamic conformations can be functional. Mature proteins need not all be rigid compact globules.
C
A mutant DnaK binds ATP and peptide but hydrolyzes ATP slowly. Which immediate effect is most plausible?
Reduced ability to retain vulnerable segments|A universal block in aminoacylation|Permanent locking in the ADP state|Loss of all ER glycans
A
Slow ATP hydrolysis impairs transition from rapidly exchanging ATP-bound state to longer-lived ADP-bound retention. It does not cause an ADP trap or directly inhibit tRNA charging or glycosylation.
C
A GrpE-defective bacterial strain has abundant soluble DnaK-bound client but little free active enzyme. What is the best working hypothesis?
The client was never translated|ADP release and substrate release are impaired|GroES has been synthesized in the ER|The peptide backbone has been universally cleaved
B
A nucleotide exchange defect can prolong client residence in ADP-bound DnaK. Client detection contradicts no translation; ER localization and universal cleavage are unsupported.
C
A GroEL mutant captures substrate normally but cannot bind GroES. Which step is most directly affected?
Transcription initiation|tRNA aminoacylation|Chamber closure and normal encapsulation|Cytosolic N-linked glycan trimming
C
Recruitment precedes GroES-mediated closure. A defect in capping need not impair initial substrate capture or RNA/tRNA reactions.
C
A labeled mitochondrial protein enters the matrix in both control and Hsp60-defective yeast, but only control forms an active oligomer. Which is best supported?
Hsp60 is a mitochondrial DNA polymerase|Import failed in the mutant|Hsp60 necessarily is a permanent subunit|Hsp60 contributes to post-import folding or assembly
D
Import is preserved in the stated experiment. Loss of mature oligomer localizes the defect downstream; permanent incorporation or DNA synthesis is not demonstrated.
C
Two synonymous variants produce equal mRNA and equal newly synthesized protein, yet one has lower native enzyme yield and altered local elongation. What inference is strongest?

Translation timing may influence folding despite identical amino acid sequence|The genetic code assigns different amino acids here|All synonymous changes reduce folding|The slower variant must always fold better
A
The equal primary sequence and synthesis support investigating a timing-dependent effect, though additional controls are needed. Direction and universality cannot be assumed.
C
A protein has eight distinct cysteines, all paired intramolecularly. How many unrestricted complete pairings are possible?
B
Choose a partner for a designated cysteine in 7 ways, then 5, then 3, then 1: 105. Counting 8! overcounts order and orientation; 16 and 64 do not follow the pairing rule.
C
A client is 80% soluble but only 25% of the control specific activity is recovered. Assuming unchanged catalytic activity per native molecule, what follows?
Every soluble molecule is native|The protein must have been mistranslated|Solubility and functional maturation are not equivalent|The fraction active must equal 80%
C
Soluble nonnative intermediates or chaperone-bound molecules can remain. The activity and solubility results are distinct; mistranslation is not established.
C
Under a first-order competing-path model kf = 0.3 min⁻¹ and ka = 0.2 min⁻¹. What is the long-time productive fraction?
D
The ratio kf/(kf+ka) = 0.3/0.5 = 0.6. A rate constant by itself is not a dimensionless yield; the ratio kf/ka is not the competing-path fraction.
C
In that model, a holdase lowers ka from 0.2 to 0.05 min⁻¹ with kf fixed at 0.3 min⁻¹. What is the new yield?
Approximately 85.7%|50%|15%|100%
A
0.3/0.35 ≈ 0.857. Competing loss remains nonzero, so yield is not 100%; the rate reduction cannot be read directly as a percentage yield.
C
For U → F and U → A, with kf+ka = 0.4 min⁻¹, what is the half-time for U disappearance?
0.4 min|1.73 min|2.5 min exactly|4 min
B
t½ = ln2/0.4 = 1.733 min. The reciprocal 2.5 min is the exponential time constant, not half-time.
C
For productive rate kf U and aggregation-associated loss 2k2 U², doubling U changes their ratio (aggregation loss/productive rate) by what factor?
One half|Four|Two|Unchanged
C
The ratio is 2k2 U/kf, linear in U. Aggregation rate quadruples but productive rate doubles, so the ratio doubles.
C
A protein needs two A and one B subunits. There are 180 mature A and 80 mature B molecules. What is the maximum number of complexes?
D
min(floor(180/2),80) = 80. B is limiting, leaving 20 A molecules. 90 assumes more B than available.
C
In a nonreducing SDS gel, a protein migrates near 72 kDa; reducing conditions reveal 50 and 22 kDa chains. Best interpretation?

A disulfide-linked heterodimer is consistent with these observations|A single intrachain disulfide necessarily splits the peptide backbone|The two chains must be translated by the same ribosome|The native complex must contain exactly four subunits
A
Reduction cleaves disulfides rather than peptide bonds. A linked 50+22 kDa species is consistent; translation history and native quaternary stoichiometry are not proven by these bands alone.
C
A mutant secretory protein is ER-localized, has normal initial synthesis, but forms abnormal covalent dimers that disappear under reducing conditions. Which mechanism is favored?
Promoter deletion|Incorrect intermolecular disulfide formation|Failure to decode every stop codon|Loss of all ribosomes
B
Reducing sensitivity suggests disulfide linkages; normal synthesis and ER entry disfavor promoter or global translation loss. It does not by itself identify the precise cysteines.
C
A PDI catalytic-site variant retains client binding. It increases soluble client but not correct disulfide pairing. What is the best interpretation?
Solubility proves exchange is normal|PDI is a ribosomal protein|Binding assistance is separable from disulfide-exchange catalysis|The substrate contains no peptide bonds
C
A binding-competent catalytic mutant can protect the client without catalyzing correction. Correct pairings and activity require independent measurement.
C
After glucose removal from a nonnative ER glycoprotein, UGGT is inactivated. Which effect is most directly predicted for a dependent substrate?
All glycosylation is blocked at translation initiation|Calnexin becomes a protease|All disulfides immediately disappear|Reduced reentry into the lectin chaperone cycle
D
UGGT can restore glucose to an appropriate glycan on a nonnative client, enabling renewed lectin recognition. Its loss is not equivalent to universal loss of glycans or disulfides.
C
A proinsulin mutant reaches secretory granules and has native disulfide pairing but accumulates uncleaved precursor. Which defect is most directly suggested?
Impaired recognition or cleavage at maturation sites|A complete block in ER targeting|Lack of all Hsp70 family proteins|Loss of the genetic code
A
Localization and folding are preserved as stipulated. The late precursor accumulation points to processing, although the precise defective protease or site needs testing.
C
A mutant enzyme has native-like circular dichroism, a normal denaturing mass, but migrates as a monomer rather than active dimer. Which defect is best supported?
DNA replication failure|Quaternary assembly defect|Signal peptide cleavage in all proteins|Ribosome subunit loss
B

Native separation distinguishes oligomeric state, while chain mass and broad secondary structure may remain normal. It supports impaired interface/assembly rather than global replication or translation.
C

A pulse-chase shows equal labeled precursor at time zero. Wild type subsequently accumulates processed product, but mutant precursor disappears without product. What next test best discriminates degradation from secretion or redistribution?
Only count total ribosomes|Measure only genomic DNA|Track labeled material in additional fractions and compare degradation-sensitive conditions|Assume all disappearance equals successful cleavage
C
Recovering label across compartments and testing loss mechanisms addresses alternative explanations. Equal initial precursor rules out neither later degradation nor movement.
C
Functional protein F has steady-state value pS/kd. If S = 60 molecules/min, p = 0.5 and kd = 0.03 min⁻¹, what is F?
D
Input is 30 functional molecules/min and steady state is 30/0.03 = 1000 molecules. 30 is a flux, not a pool.
AR
Assertion: Hsp70 ATP hydrolysis can improve maturation without incorporating ATP into the client. Reason: nucleotide state controls substrate binding and release.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
A
ATP-dependent changes regulate the chaperone cycle and thus folding opportunities. The nucleotide is not a structural component of the client.
AR
Assertion: a reducing treatment can split mature insulin A and B chains under denaturing conditions. Reason: peptide bonds are routinely hydrolyzed by reducing agents.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
C
Reduction breaks interchain disulfides, not ordinary peptide backbone bonds. The assertion is true under the stated conditions, the reason false.
AR
Assertion: an enzyme can lose activity without a reduction in initial translation. Reason: proper folding and assembly may be required after synthesis.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
A
An unchanged supply of chains does not guarantee a correctly organized active protein; folding or assembly can independently limit activity.
AR
Assertion: GroES is required by every known chaperonin. Reason: eukaryotic CCT has intrinsic chamber-closing elements.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
D
Group II CCT uses an intrinsic lid mechanism rather than the bacterial GroES cochaperonin. The reason is true and the universal assertion is false.
AR
Assertion: a PPIase can accelerate recovery of a native enzyme. Reason: it lowers the kinetic barrier for cis–trans interconversion at suitable peptide bonds.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
A
The catalyst can relieve a slow conformational bottleneck without changing the primary sequence or equilibrium of an isolated isomerization reaction.
AR
Assertion: an ER glycoprotein may interact repeatedly with calnexin. Reason: every client remains permanently monoglucosylated regardless of folding state.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
C
Trimming and possible UGGT-mediated reglucosylation enable repeated rounds. The glycan is not permanently in the recognition state.
MS
Select the correct statements: I. Hsp70 can recognize exposed peptide segments. II. GroEL provides a chamber for appropriate clients. III. All newly made proteins must pass through both systems.
I and III|I and II only|II and III|All three
B
I and II describe standard mechanisms. III is false because dependence differs among substrates and organisms.
MS
Select the correct statements: I. Cytosolic disulfides are absolutely impossible. II. The ER supports oxidative folding. III. An incorrect disulfide can trap a nonnative state.
I only|I and II|II and III only|All three
C
The ER supports oxidative folding and erroneous pairings can impede maturation. Cytosolic disulfides are unusual under reducing conditions, not impossible.
MS

Select the correct statements: I. Zymogen activation often involves limited proteolysis. II. Signal cleavage and activation cleavage can solve different problems. III. Every processing event destroys the entire protein.
III only|II and III|All three|I and II only
D
Limited processing generates useful products and can regulate location or activity. III conflates processing with degradation.
MS

Select the correct statements: I. A soluble protein can be nonnative. II. A native oligomer is not necessarily an aggregate. III. The specific activity of a preparation can help estimate active fraction under stated assumptions.
I, II and III|I only|II only|I and III only
A
All three observations concern different properties and are compatible. Activity-based estimates require unchanged per-molecule activity and matched assay conditions.
M
Match 1 DnaJ, 2 GrpE, 3 GroES, 4 PDI to P nucleotide exchange, Q chamber lid, R stimulates Hsp70 hydrolysis, S disulfide exchange.
1P 2R 3S 4Q|1R 2P 3Q 4S|1Q 2P 3R 4S|1S 2Q 3P 4R
B
DnaJ stimulates ATP hydrolysis, GrpE promotes nucleotide exchange, GroES is the lid and PDI catalyzes thiol-disulfide exchange.
M
Match 1 BiP, 2 CCT, 3 Dsb system, 4 Hsp60/Hsp10 to P mitochondrial matrix, Q bacterial periplasm, R eukaryotic cytosol, S ER lumen.
1Q 2S 3R 4P|1P 2R 3S 4Q|1S 2R 3Q 4P|1R 2Q 3P 4S
C
BiP acts in ER lumen, CCT in eukaryotic cytosol, Dsb proteins in the bacterial periplasmic oxidative folding system and Hsp60/Hsp10 in the mitochondrial matrix.
M
Match 1 pulse-chase, 2 reducing SDS-PAGE, 3 native size separation, 4 activity assay to P oligomeric state estimate, Q cohort fate, R functional output, S disulfide-sensitive chain connectivity.
1S 2R 3Q 4P|1R 2P 3S 4Q|1P 2Q 3R 4S|1Q 2S 3P 4R
D

Each method answers a distinct question. Pulse-chase tracks a labeled cohort, reducing gels test certain covalent links, native size separation estimates assembly and catalytic assay reports function.
N
A translation rate is 15 residues/s. A domain needs 90 additional residues synthesized before a later interaction region emerges. Under constant speed, what is the interval?
A
90 residues divided by 15 residues/s equals 6 s. This only predicts the time interval, not folding probability.
N
From 250 correctly folded proinsulin molecules, 80% are fully processed by the normal pathway. Ignoring clearance, how many insulin and C-peptide molecules result?
250 each|200 each|400 insulin and 200 C-peptide|200 insulin and no C-peptide
B
250 × 0.8 = 200 processing events; each produces one insulin and one C-peptide. The other values violate the stated conversion fraction or stoichiometry.
N
A reconstituted system hydrolyzes 450 ATP while 150 molecules become active. What is the measured system-level ATP-to-product ratio?
0.33 ATP/product|150 ATP/product|3 ATP/product|450 ATP/product
C
450/150 = 3 ATP per active product on average for the whole system. It does not establish exactly three cycles for every client.
N
In a hypothetical paired assay, sample A contains 40 μg enzyme and produces 80 units of activity; sample B contains 50 μg and produces 25 units. Relative apparent specific activity of B vs A?
D
A = 80/40 = 2 units/μg; B = 25/50 = 0.5 units/μg. The ratio is 0.25. Comparing raw activity alone gives 31.25%, which ignores enzyme mass.
